newsitem.title: FINLAND: M-Serla sees upturn slow to bear fruit.
newsitem.headline: M-Serla sees upturn slow to bear fruit.

text.p: Finnish forestry group Metsa-Serla Oy said on Monday it expected business to start recovering in 1997, but the positive impact on earnings was only likely to show in 1998.
"A turn for the better will probably happen this year," Metsa-Serla said in a statement with its 1996 results. "But the results will only be reaped in the next financial year."
Metsa-Serla said the fall last year in product prices had come to a halt, but prices were not expected to strengthen significantly this spring.
"The best part of 1997 must be seen through based on the prices prevailing after the sharp fall last year," it said.
Demand for forest industry products was on the rise, but so was supply and capacity utilisation was not expected to improve in the near future, the company said.
Mainly due to the fall in pulp and paper prices, Metsa-Serla's 1996 profit after financial items fell to 315 million markka from 1.91 billion markka in 1995. @
